concerns.text: The target variable is defined as an effort‑adjusted cumulative‑count threshold (scaled by the per‑cell effort covariate) and then the same effort covariate is also used as a predictor in the secondary model. Even though the primary model omits the covariate, the target itself still embeds effort information, which can re‑introduce circularity and bias environmental effect estimates (construct‑validity issue).

The Diebold‑Mariano test is applied to compare model prediction errors, but DM is designed for time‑series forecast evaluation, not for spatially structured predictions. Even with HAC correction, the test may not adequately account for spatial autocorrelation, potentially inflating type‑I error rates.
